title: UQ Salary Scales: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using UQ salary scales. Includes formula, fortnightly pay, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you are casual, remember that your hourly rate may already include a 25% loading – check your pay slip or agreement. The timesheet on this site lets you enter a base rate and optionally add casual loading.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour; with 25% loading it becomes $33.05. The UQ salary scales already include this loading in their published casual rates, so if you use those rates directly, do not add loading again. Our timesheet has a checkbox to add the 25% loading separately when you enter a base rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for the 2026-27 year is $270,830. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 in super. Our estimates use this 12% rate, but always check your award or agreement for the correct rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding UQ Salary Scales and Annual Pay Conversion

If you are a casual academic or professional staff member at the University of Queensland, you have likely come across the **UQ salary scales** – a detailed schedule of hourly and annual rates set by the University’s Enterprise Agreement 2021–2026. These scales are a great example of how to convert an hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. This article explains the conversion formula, the role of casual loading, superannuation, and tax, using the UQ salary scales as a reference.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The standard way to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the standard under the National Employment Standards), this becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, a UQ professional staff member at HEW Level 3.01 (from 11 July 2026) earns $46.47 per hour casual. Their annual equivalent would be $46.47 × 38 × 52 = $91,824.72. However, note that this is a notional figure – casual employees do not receive paid leave, and the rate already includes a 25% casual loading.

### Fortnightly Pay

To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same example: weekly pay = $46.47 × 38 = $1,765.86; fortnightly = $3,531.72. This matches the UQ salary scales which list full-time fortnightly rates for each salary point.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs UQ Rates

It is important to distinguish between different pay standards:

- **National Minimum Wage**: From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.
- **Award Rates**: Many industries have specific awards that set minimum pay rates higher than the national minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award.
- **UQ Salary Scales**: These are set by the University’s enterprise agreement, approved by the Fair Work Commission. They are generally higher than award rates. For example, a casual academic delivering a basic lecture (AC10A) from 11 July 2026 earns $238.22 for a 3-hour minimum engagement, which equates to $79.41 per hour. Professional staff at HEW Level 1.01 casual rate is $41.84 per hour – well above the national minimum.

### Casual Loading and the UQ Scales

The UQ salary scales explicitly state: “The rates listed here incorporate 25% loading.” This means if you are using those published rates, you should **not** add casual loading again. Our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add 25% loading on top of a base rate. If you enter a UQ casual rate, leave the checkbox unchecked. For award or minimum wage rates, you would check it to include loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is calculated at 12% of your ordinary time earnings (from 1 July 2026) and is paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It does not come out of your pay. The maximum contribution base for the 2026–27 year is $270,830. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 in super. Our estimates use this 12% rate, but always check your agreement – UQ’s super contribution may vary.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimates use these rates, but note that the Medicare levy surcharge and HELP repayments are not included.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is designed to help you convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and optionally add casual loading. The calculator will show gross annual pay, estimated super, and tax. For UQ staff, you can directly enter the hourly rate from the UQ salary scales (which already include loading) and leave the casual loading checkbox unchecked.

### Reference Tables and Pay Guides

For more detailed comparisons, see our [reference tables](/data) which list the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and common salary scales. You can also browse [pay guides](/blog) for industry-specific information. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how loading works across different awards.

### Conclusion

The UQ salary scales provide a clear example of how hourly rates translate to annual pay. Remember the formula: hourly × hours per week × 52. Always check whether your rate already includes casual loading, and remember that super is paid on top. Use our tools to estimate your take-home pay, and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or your enterprise agreement for exact entitlements.
